# DSH ChatGPT Adapter

**把 ChatGPT 订阅带进 DeepSeek Harness。登录账户，选择 GPT，即可开始工作。** 无需 API Key，支持 GPT / DeepSeek 切换、图片理解，以及 Harness 的文件、搜索和终端工具。 **仅适用于 DeepSeek Harness。** 本插件不能安装到 DeepSeek 普通网页版、手机 App 或普通聊天桌面客户端中。支持 Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS；当前实测基线为 0.2.0-rc.2。 [快速开始](#快速开始) · [使用文档](docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [下载安装包](https://github.com/diwer/dsh-codex-adapter/releases/latest) · [English](README.en.md) ## 为什么使用 - **用自己的订阅**：通过 OpenAI 页面登录授权，无需配置 API Key。 - **两种模型，随时选择**：在会话中切换 GPT 与 DeepSeek，也可让新会话默认使用 GPT。 - **图片与工具一起用**：向支持图片的模型提问，使用 Harness 内置工具读取文件、编辑代码、搜索和运行命令。 - **思考强度可调**：在模型菜单中选择推理等级，档位与默认值自动匹配当前模型。 - **连接后即可选模型**：自动加载当前账户的可用模型，支持添加和切换多个账户。 - **插件独立代理**：在订阅设置页选择直连、环境变量或自定义 HTTP(S) 代理，支持测试连接，保存后立即生效。 - **免费开源**：MIT 许可；插件不额外收费。模型权限与使用额度取决于你的 ChatGPT 账户。 ## 快速开始 适用于 **DeepSeek Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS**，需要可使用订阅模型的 ChatGPT 账户。 ### 1. 安装插件 在 **Plugins → Add plugin** 中填入： ```text dsh-codex-official-adapter@0.1.8 ``` Registry 选择 **npm 官方源（https://registry.npmjs.org/）**，点击 **Install**。完成后，等当前任务结束，完全退出并重新打开 Harness。 > 若找不到切换源的入口，或安装失败，使用[终端安装或本地包安装](docs/INSTALLATION.md#其他安装方式)。 ### 2. 连接 ChatGPT 打开 **Settings → ChatGPT 订阅 → 连接 ChatGPT**，点击 **打开授权页面**，在 OpenAI 页面完成登录与授权。返回 Harness 后会自动显示连接状态和可用模型。 ### 3. 开始使用 新建会话，在模型选择器的 **ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT)** 下选择模型。 试着输入：`帮我阅读当前项目，说明它的用途。` 支持图片的模型也可以直接接收会话中添加的图片。 ## 常见问题 **这个插件支持哪个产品？** 仅支持 DeepSeek Harness。DeepSeek 普通网页版、手机 App 和普通聊天桌面客户端不支持安装本插件。支持 Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS；当前实测基线为 0.2.0-rc.2。 **如何在 DeepSeek Harness 中使用 ChatGPT 订阅？** 安装 `dsh-codex-official-adapter@0.1.8`，在设置中连接自己的 ChatGPT 账户，再从 ChatGPT plan 中选择模型。无需 API Key，模型权限与额度由账户决定。 **可以直接填 GitHub 地址吗？** 这是源码地址：`https://github.com/diwer/dsh-codex-adapter`。不同宿主与市场的安装器支持有差异，日常安装建议使用上面的明确包名与版本。 **已经连接，却没有模型？** 点击“刷新模型”，检查当前账户的订阅权限、额度及网络。模型列表以账户实际返回为准。 **如何升级？** 用相同包名安装新版本，然后完全退出并重开 Harness。保留原 Profile 和账户目录即可延续使用。 **如何退出或卸载？** 先在设置页退出账户，再到 Plugins 卸载。[详细说明](docs/PRIVACY.md#断开与卸载)。 ## 了解更多 [思考强度](docs/REASONING.md) · [安装与排错](docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [兼容范围](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [数据与隐私](docs/PRIVACY.md) · [版本说明](RELEASE_NOTES.md) · [参与开发](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) 会话文本、所选图片和工具结果会发送至 OpenAI。登录凭证保存在本机未加密文件中，具有仅当前用户可读写的权限。本插件是独立社区项目，不隶属于 OpenAI 或 DeepSeek。 ### 插件头像 启用插件后，窗口右下角会显示「大肥鱼指挥 Codex」头像。图片随安装包提供，无需外部图片服务；头像不响应鼠标操作，不遮挡下方控件的点击。停用插件后自动移除。

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: DSH guard against self-repetition in streamed model output: detects a degeneration loop in reasoning or visible text, aborts the runaway turn and wakes the agent with a corrective notice.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-output-loop-guard

An **output self-repetition watchdog** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/).
When a model starts cycling the same short block instead of producing a tool call, the guard
aborts that generation and wakes the agent with a corrective notice — no human stop button,
and no human typing "continue".

- Bundle for DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2`, ESM, zero runtime dependencies.
- 21 self-contained regression checks (`npm test`).
- Calibrated against 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps: **24 detections, 0 false positives**.

## The gap it fills

DSH ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-repeat-tool-reminder`, which only sees **duplicate tool calls**
(same tool, same arguments, 3/5/8 times in a row). A degeneration loop in the *reasoning
channel* is invisible to it. In the session that motivated this plugin:

- the model repeated `好。→（执行）→好。→Write.→…` in its reasoning for **112,109 characters**,
  emitted in **50,196 stream chunks over 126 seconds of continuous decoding**, and produced
  **zero tool calls** — so `repeat-tool-reminder` could not fire;
- automatic compaction never ran either: its trigger is
  `floor(min(W × 0.8, W − O − B))` ≈ 678k tokens for a 1M window with a 256k output cap,
  while the session peaked around 508k tokens;
- the loop only ended when the human pressed stop, and the polluted text stayed in the
  transcript, which made further loops more likely (self-imitation).

`output-loop-guard` listens on the live `agent/assistant-stream` frames and looks at the text itself.

## How it works

A sliding window over streamed output (1,200 characters by default, inspected every 64 new
characters) feeds four signals:

| Signal | Rule | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `repeated-block` | **Shortest-period** block (≥2 newlines, ≥2 distinct non-whitespace chars) repeated ≥6 times | Multi-line cycles, e.g. the 106-character `好。→（执行）→Write.` cycle |
| `dominant-gram` | One n-gram covers ≥55% of the window with ≥24 occurrences and spans ≥2 lines | Loops whose tail is ragged but where repetition already dominates |
| `repeated-line` | Single-line runs: ≥40 in the reasoning channel, ≥60 in visible text (`singleLineTextMinRepeats`, `0` disables) | Reasoning spinning on one line, runaway line duplication in answers |
| `flat-tic` | Whitespace-free short gram covering ≥25% of the window with ≥48 occurrences, **reasoning only** | Line-less tics (`好。好。好。…`) |

Two design rules keep it precise:

- **Only the shortest period counts.** When one line repeats, 2× and 3× the line length are also
  "periods"; judging on an arbitrary period turned an ordinary bullet list into a "multi-line
  cycle" during calibration. The guard therefore looks only at the shortest period and requires
  that block itself to span ≥2 newlines.
- **Channel awareness.** Repeated lines in visible output are usually legitimate content
  (generated fixtures, config files, lists), so the visible-text single-line threshold is higher
  (60) than the reasoning one (40), and line-less tics are only judged in the reasoning channel.
  Indentation runs, `====` / `----` rule lines and blank-line runs never trip the guard.

On detection the guard:

1. calls `agent.cancel({ kind: 'hook', reason: 'output-loop-guard: …' })` — the in-flight
   generation is aborted and recorded as interrupted, so the degenerate text stops growing;
2. calls `agent.steer(<notice>)` — because the signal is already aborted, `steer` upgrades to a
   **fresh turn** and wakes the driver, so the agent immediately continues with an explicit
   correction (stop restating, emit the next action or finish);
3. after `maxTripsPerTurn` trips in one turn it stops auto-continuing and only `inject`s the
   notice, so a genuinely broken model cannot spin forever.

## Install

The package is a DSH **bundle**: the loader reads `dsh.bundle.patch` from `package.json`
(`dsh.plugin.json` is optional metadata used by some local plugin indexes — the official runtime
ignores it), and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `output-loop-guard` row.

```sh
# A. from a git host, pinned to a commit (requires `git` on the PATH of the DSH process)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "github:ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard#<commit>"

# B. from the release tarball — no git required
#    download dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz from the Releases page, then:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz

# C. straight from the release asset URL (needs Node to trust your system CA store)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  https://github.com/ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz
```

All three append the package to `dsh.profile.bundles` and compose the bundle's patch layer.
**Restart DSH for the row to activate.**

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-output-loop-guard
```

## Configuration

Override the row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`,
so restate every key you want to keep):

```yaml
- id: output-loop-guard
  name: dsh-output-loop-guard
  config:
    dryRun: false                 # true = detect and log only, never cancel
    autoContinue: true            # wake the agent with the corrective notice
    maxTripsPerTurn: 2            # auto-continue budget per turn
    windowChars: 1200
    checkEveryChars: 64
    minPeriodRepeats: 6           # repeats required for a multi-line cycle
    singleLineMinRepeats: 40      # reasoning-channel single-line threshold
    singleLineTextMinRepeats: 60  # visible-text single-line threshold (0 = off)
    useDominantGram: true
    dominantGramCoverage: 0.55
    dominantGramMinCount: 24
    useFlatTic: true
    ticMinCount: 48
    ticMinCoverage: 0.25
    verbose: false
```

Start with `dryRun: true` if you want to observe detections in your own sessions before letting
the guard abort anything.

## Evidence

### Corpus calibration

Replayed over 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps (a corpus containing both healthy and
degenerate real output):

- 24 detections, **0 false positives**;
- every loop step of the motivating session was caught, plus a same-pattern loop in an unrelated
  session;
- detection latency: the 112,109-character runaway was caught after **2,944 characters (2.6 %)**;
  other loops were caught within 1,152–7,808 characters — hundreds of milliseconds instead of
  20–126 seconds of spinning.

### Runtime verification

End-to-end check in a live DSH runtime, on a task engineered to repeat two lines 300 times. The
session log of that run contains:

```json
{"type":"turn/end","data":{"turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"aborted","reason":{"kind":"hook","reason":"output-loop-guard: repeated output (repeated-block)"}}}}
{"type":"assistant/message","interrupted":true}          // cut off after 9 repetitions, not 300
{"type":"user/message","source":{"kind":"output-loop-guard","form":"notice"}}
```

The agent then delivered the same content as a **file** instead of continuing to repeat it, which
is exactly the intended outcome: the guard stops runaway output, it does not kill the task.

### Regression suite

`npm test` runs 21 self-contained checks (no corpus needed): the real degeneracy must be aborted
(24,180-character stream caught after 576 characters), healthy long documents must be untouched,
realistic written output (lists, code blocks, tables, rule lines, fixtures) must not trip,
runaway written lines must trip, `dryRun` must not cancel, a disabled plugin must attach nothing,
and a throwing agent handle must not break the stream.

## Limitations

- Visible-text single-line repetition needs ≥60 identical consecutive lines (that protects
  legitimate fixtures and lists); disable with `singleLineTextMinRepeats: 0`.
- Detection is structural (periodicity and density), not semantic: a modified near-repeat may
  escape `repeated-block`, though `dominant-gram` / `flat-tic` usually covers it.
- Trips are counted per agent and per attempt; subagents do not share counters.
- A trip discards the tool call that step had not emitted yet — one retry is the price for not
  spinning for minutes. Use `dryRun` to observe first.

#

plugins.description: Adds a Restart row to the desktop app's sidebar foot beside Settings that restarts the app and reloads the page onto the newly installed plugin bundle.
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-sidebar-restart One row in the sidebar foot, beside the settings gear: restarts the DSH desktop app in a single click, instead of quitting from the tray and relaunching by hand. ![The Restart row above Settings in the desktop app](docs/usage-desktop.png) ![The same row in the mobile drawer, label included](docs/usage-phone.png) [![三种形态](docs/placement-options.png)](docs/placement-options.png) ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-sidebar-restart # once it is on npm ``` or straight from the repository: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:DONGBIN007/dsh-sidebar-restart ``` Then restart the app once by hand so the plugin loads — which is the last time you have to do that, since this button is what you use from then on. **Desktop only.** On a plain `dsh web` profile the row renders disabled and says why; there is no desktop process to replace there. If you wanted the *Web server* restarted, that is a different plugin ([`dsh-restart-button`](https://github.com/hadesybil-hub/dsh-restart-button)). ## What it does, in one line Adds a **Restart** row to the desktop app's sidebar foot beside Settings. Clicking it asks the Host to restart; a detached helper kills the Electron main process and the Host by PID, waits until both are gone, starts the app again, and the tab reloads itself once the replacement answers with a new boot id — so a plugin you installed a moment ago is actually running afterwards. ## What it looks like | Desktop app (wide sidebar) | Mobile drawer | |---|---| | ![desktop](docs/usage-desktop.png) | ![mobile](docs/usage-phone.png) | Both follow the host's own rule rather than a breakpoint of mine: the label appears exactly where the host shows one for the gear, i.e. when the sidebar is wide. In the narrow 56px rail the row stays icon-only and keeps the gear's 36×36 target. ## The control is a copy of the gear row next door The seat is `sidebar.footer.action` — "optional actions beside Settings at the sidebar foot". The shipped sidebar renders it as `footerActions`, a flex row that `footArea` lays out **above** `settingsArea` (the gear row). So in the plain host footer this control sits directly above the gear. It is deliberately styled as the gear's twin, with every value read from the shipped `.wCInkW_trigger` (ui-settings-general) and the seat's own sibling `.dsh-mobile-control__trigger`, which agree: | Property | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | colour | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` | the gear uses the **primary** label colour; a secondary-coloured icon beside it is a visible mismatch | | height | `42px` | the footer row height both host controls use | | padding | `0 10px 0 8px`, `gap 8px` | the gear's own padding and icon/label gap | | radius | `--dsw-radius-md` | the gear's radius, not the small one | | label | `14px / 22px`, `font: inherit` | the gear label's typography | | row box | `calc(100% + 4px)`, `margin 4px -2px` | the gear's row is `.wCInkW_triggerRow{width:calc(100% + 4px);margin:4px -2px}` — it bleeds 2px past the column on each side, so its content begins at `parentLeft − 2 + 8 = +6`. Without the same bleed this row's icon **and** label sit 2px to the right of the gear's, and the two never line up. This button *is* its own row, so it carries both the bleed and the padding. | Verified on a **real phone screenshot** (1216×2640, so ≈3.5 device px per CSS px), measuring the dark ink of each row directly: | row, on the device | icon ink left | label ink left | icon ink | row centre | |---|---|---|---|---| | before the bleed: 重启 | `73` | `157` | 50 | `2356.5` | | before the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 | `2531.5` | | after the bleed: 重启 | `66` | `150` | 50 | — | | after the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 | — | So the old geometry sat **+6 device px (≈2 CSS px)** right of the gear — the 2px the CSS predicted — and the shipped geometry lands within **1 device px** on the icon and **exactly 0** on the label. The two row centres are 175 device px apart, which is `175 / 3.5 = 50.0` CSS px — precisely the designed `21 + 4 + 4 + 21`. [![真机对齐：橙色线为齿轮图标左缘](docs/row-alignment-device.png)](docs/row-alignment-device.png) The orange line is the gear's own icon left edge. Before, the ↻ icon and the 重启 label both sit to its right; after, they land on it. The equivalent check against the host's shipped CSS in a controlled 340px column gives the same result to the hundredth: | row | icon left | label left | |---|---|---| | the gear | `5.67` | `29.67` | | this button, before the bleed | `7.67` (**+2.00**) | `31.67` (**+2.00**) | | this button, after the bleed | `5.67` (**0.00**) | `29.67` (**0.00**) | [![受控 CSS 校验](docs/row-alignment.png)](docs/row-alignment.png) One residual is **not** a CSS mismatch and is deliberately left alone: on the device the ↻ ink is 50px against the gear's 48px. Both icons are the host's own primitives at the host's own `wide ? 16 : 18`, drawn on the same 16px box with the same 1.3 stroke — a near-full circle simply carries more ink than a compact gear. Making the two inks match would mean drawing the shipped artwork below the size the host asks for, which is the one thing this row must not do. **The label follows the host's own `wide` convention** — no invented breakpoint. The gear's `TriggerContent` renders `wide ? + label : `, and `dsh-mobile`, the seat's other occupant, does `wide ?

plugins.description: DSH plugin: auto-compact long sessions after user idle time, before the KV cache expires.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-idle-compact [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that prepares a compaction of a long session while you are away, before the model provider's KV cache expires, and lets you apply it with one click when you come back.

## Why

Providers cache the prompt prefix of a conversation for a few minutes. While the cache is warm, re-reading a long history is cheap. Once it expires, your next message re-bills the whole history at the full, uncached input price.

If you walk away from a long session, this plugin produces the compaction summary while the cache is still warm, so that summarization request is cheap. Nothing changes in your session until you decide to apply it.

## How it works

1. When a session finishes a turn and waits for you, a timer starts.
2. Any new activity in that session cancels the timer, whether it's you replying or the agent starting work.
3. When the timer fires, the plugin prepares a compaction only if all of these hold:
   - the agent is still idle and its last turn finished normally (not an error or a stop);
   - no background job or subagent is running for the session;
   - the session's context, measured with DSH's token meter, has reached the threshold.
4. Preparing runs exactly the summarization request DSH's `/compact` would make, and keeps the result. Your session is not changed.
5. An **Apply compaction** bar appears just above the message input, showing how many history items it covers.
6. Clicking it runs DSH's own `/compact` command, exactly as if you had typed it, and answers its summarization request with the prepared result, so no new model call is made. The conversation shows the usual `/compact` card with its "Compacted N history items" reply.

The prepared summary is only valid for the conversation it summarized. If you send another message (or the history changes in any other way), it is discarded and the button disappears; the next idle period that qualifies prepares a fresh one. If the conversation somehow differs at the moment you click, `/compact` makes its own model call instead of using a stale summary.

When the plugin starts or is reloaded (a DSH restart, a plugin update), sessions that are already waiting are timed from the end of their last turn. A session idle for less than the idle delay is timed for only the remaining seconds. A session idle for longer is skipped entirely, because the provider's cache has most likely expired and preparing would cost full price. It qualifies again after its next turn.

Subagent sessions are skipped, because they never wait for a user reply. If the agent is busy when the timer fires, nothing is prepared and this is logged.

## Settings

Open **Plugins → Idle Compact** in the DSH Web UI:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Context length threshold (tokens) | `256000` | Prepare a compaction only when the session context has reached this length. |
| Idle time (seconds) | `300` (5 min) | How long you must go without replying before a compaction is prepared. |

Both fields take whole numbers of at least 1. Changes apply without a restart. A changed idle time takes effect the next time a session starts waiting.

You can also set them in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: idle-compact
  config:
    contextThresholdTokens: 200000
    idleSeconds: 240
```

## Install

Requires the DSH Web UI. Tested on DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3 and 0.2.1-rc.2; earlier versions are untested. The plugin uses DSH's authenticated `/api` routes, its settings-form components, and the area above the message input (`conversation.input.dock`).

```sh
dsh plugin add github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact
```

Or, in the Web UI, open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact` or a local checkout path.

## Token cost

Each prepared compaction makes one summarization call to your model. It's cheap because the cache is warm, but it is spent even if you never click Apply or never return to that session. If most of your idle sessions are ones you abandon, raise the threshold.

Prepared summaries are kept in memory only. Restarting DSH discards them.

## Page endpoints

The browser half talks to the Host over two routes on DSH's own `/api` channel. DSH checks the browser's login and origin before either route runs, so other programs and other websites can't use them.

- `GET /api/idle-compact/events?sessionId=<id>`: a server-sent event stream. The first message is the session's current state, and another follows each change. Each message is `{ "prepared": false }`, or `{ "prepared": true, "items": <history items>, "tokens": <approx. tokens>, "applying": <boolean> }`.
- `POST /api/idle-compact/apply` with JSON `{ "sessionId": "<id>" }` applies the prepared compaction. Responses:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | `{ "ok": <boolean>, "result": <command result> }` | `/compact` ran; `ok` is whether it succeeded. Its outcome also shows in the chat. |
| 200 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "command-unavailable" }` | The `/compact` command isn't available. |
| 400 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "bad-body" }` | The body isn't a JSON object with a non-empty string `sessionId`. |
| 404 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "no-session" }` | No live session has that id. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "not-prepared" }` | Nothing is prepared, or it went stale. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "applying" }` | An apply is already running for that session. |
| 500 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "failed", "message": "…" }` | Applying failed unexpectedly. |

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

The tests load the plugin into a real DSH runtime from your local DSH install and fake only the model provider and the browser connection. Set `DSH_RUNTIME_DIRS` (colon-separated `node_modules/@deepseek-ai` directories) to choose which runtimes to test against.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: settings schema, public exports, and wiring of the parts below. |
| `src/idle-scheduler.js` | One idle timer per agent; aborts its work when the agent resumes. |
| `src/prepare.js` | Eligibility checks, and producing the summary on a detached copy of the session. |
| `src/replay.js` | Records the summarization request while preparing; replays it once on apply. |
| `src/prepared-store.js` | What is prepared for each session, and notifying the page when it changes. |
| `src/http.js` | The page's endpoints on DSH's authenticated `/api` channel. |
| `src/constants.js`, `src/util.js` | Shared names, values, and small helpers. |
| `client.js` | Browser half: the settings form on the Plugins page and the Apply bar above the message input. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `idle-compact` row. |
| `locale/*.json`, `icon.svg` | Display metadata for the plugin manager. |
| `test/` | Tests that run the plugin inside a real DSH runtime. |

## License

MIT

plugins.description: DSH web_fetch fallback: when AnySearch extraction fails with HTTP 422, the page is fetched directly with a browser-like user agent. Zero-dependency DSH plugin.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-anysearch-fallback

**给 DSH 的 `web_fetch` 加一条降级兜底：AnySearch 抽不出内容（HTTP 422）时，自动改用浏览器 UA 直抓。**
*Gives DSH's `web_fetch` a fallback: when AnySearch cannot extract a page (HTTP 422), fetch it directly with a browser-like user agent instead of failing the whole call.*

[中文](#中文) · [English](#english)

---

## 中文

### 它解决什么问题

DSH 的 `web_fetch` 走 AnySearch 的 `/v1/extract`。有些页面（`openai.com`、知乎问题页、不存在的路径……）上游会返回 **HTTP 422 `extract_failed`**，于是整次 `web_fetch` 直接报错。本插件在那个位置接一手：先照旧走 AnySearch，**上游一失败就直抓原文兜底**（唯一例外是"取消"），并在正文首行写明上游失败的真实原因。

### 工作机制

```
ctx.web 注册的 provider 链：
  anysearch-fallback (provider id: anysearch-fallback)   ← web_fetch 选中它
        │
        ├─ 代理到官方 AnySearch provider 的 extract
        │     ├─ 成功 → 原样返回（逐字段不变）
        │     ├─ 任何失败（422 / 401 / 402 / 403 / 429 / 超时 / 网络…）→ 进入直抓兜底
        │     │     兜底结果的正文首行写明上游失败原因（状态 + 摘要）
        │     └─ 取消 / abort → 原样抛错，绝不降级（调用方已要求停止）
        │
        └─ 直抓兜底：浏览器 UA + 协议/内网校验 + 5 MB 字节上限 + 15s 超时
              → 返回带标记的纯文本（正文顶部写入降级标记，模型一眼可辨）
```

- 本插件**不修改**官方 `@anysearch/anysearch-dsh` 的任何文件，也不改 DSH 私有字段；它以自己的 id `anysearch-fallback` 注册 provider，内部再按 id 调官方 `anysearch` provider。
- 官方插件升级/重装对本插件**无影响**（若官方改了 provider id，需要同步改 `index.mjs` 里的 `UPSTREAM_PROVIDER_ID`）。
- 兜底失败时，抛出的错误里同时带上「上游原始错误」与「直抓失败原因」+ 一句可行动提示，两侧信息都不吞。

### 关键行为

| 项目 | 取值 |
| --- | --- |
| provider id | `anysearch-fallback`（由本插件的 `- id: web` 覆盖把 `fetchProvider` 指到它；上游仍是官方 `anysearch`） |
| 触发降级 | **任何上游错误**：422 / 401（凭据）/ 402（额度）/ 403 / 429（限流）/ 5xx / 超时 / 网络错误 / 非 JSON 响应，无一例外 |
| 不降级（唯一例外） | **取消 / abort**：调用方的 `signal` 已中止，或错误链上有 `name: AbortError`、`code: ABORT_ERR / WEB_ABORTED / extract_canceled`、消息含 `abort`/`cancel` → 原样抛，不直抓 |
| 协议白名单 | 仅 `http:` / `https:`（`file:` / `data:` / `ftp:` / `blob:` 等拒绝） |
| 内网拒绝 | `localhost` / `*.localhost` / `*.local` / `.internal`；IPv4 `0.0.0.0`、`127/8`、`10/8`、`172.16/12`、`192.168/16`、`169.254/16`、`100.64/10`；IPv6 `::1`、`fc00::/7`、`fe80::/10`；IPv4-mapped IPv6（`::ffff:127.0.0.1`） |
| 字节上限 | 5 MB，流式读取（`response.body`），超限立即 `cancel()` |
| 字符上限 | 与 DSH 工具侧一致（`DEFAULT_FETCH_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS`），超出裁剪并置 `truncated: true` |
| 超时 | 自带 15s，串联上游 `signal`，任一触发即中止并说明来源 |
| 请求头 | 固定桌面 Chrome UA + `accept` + `accept-language`；**不带** Authorization / Cookie / Referer |
| 重定向 | `redirect: 'manual'`，最多 3 跳，**每一跳都重做协议与内网校验** |
| 磁盘缓存 | 无 |

### 降级标记（永远在返回正文的第一行）

标记会写明**上游失败的真实原因**（状态 + 截断到 240 字符的摘要）和**直抓实际拿到的状态**；正文为空时说清"没有正文"，免得"只有一行标记"被读成"这页面是空的"。

| 情形 | 第一行 |
| --- | --- |
| 上游 422，直抓 2xx 有正文 | `[anysearch-fallback] 上游抽取失败（HTTP 422）：AnySearch extract failed: … (HTTP 422, auth credential)；直抓成功（HTTP 200），以下为未经 AnySearch 清洗的直抓原文。` |
| 上游 429，直抓 2xx 有正文 | `[anysearch-fallback] 上游错误（HTTP 429 rate limit）：AnySearch extract failed: "too many requests"；直抓成功（HTTP 200），以下为未经 AnySearch 清洗的直抓原文。` |
| 直抓非 2xx，有正文 | `[anysearch-fallback] 上游错误（HTTP 429 rate limit）：…；直抓返回 HTTP 403（站点可能拒绝匿名访问），以下为站点返回的原始内容，未经 AnySearch 清洗。` |
| 直抓非 2xx，正文为空 | `[anysearch-fallback] 上游错误（HTTP 429 rate limit）：…；直抓返回 HTTP 403 且站点未返回任何正文内容（该页可能需要登录或被反爬拦截，建议换来源）。` |
| 直抓 2xx，正文为空 | `[anysearch-fallback] 上游错误（HTTP 500）：…；直抓成功（HTTP 200）但站点未返回任何正文内容（可能是空页或正文由脚本渲染，建议换来源）。` |

- 状态取上游错误里真实的 `httpStatus`；命中"抽取失败"那三种精确形状（`httpStatus === 422` / `errorCode` 字段值 `extract_failed` / 那句 `Unable to extract content from the URL.`）时措辞为**上游抽取失败**，否则为**上游错误**（并在拿得到时附上 `rate limit` / `auth credential` 这类标签）。
- 摘要**压平空白并截断**到 240 字符（`MAX_MARKER_UPSTREAM_CHARS`），标记行因此永远是一眼能读完的一行，不是日志。
- 每次降级还会记一条 `warn` 日志（含上游原因与直抓结果）。

### 安装

作为本地插件挂进某个 DSH profile：

```bash
# 1) 把本目录放到 <DSH_HOME>/plugins/dsh-anysearch-fallback/
# 2) 在 profile 的 package.json 里加依赖（相对路径写法）
#    "dsh-anysearch-fallback": "file:C:/Users/you/.dsh/plugins/dsh-anysearch-fallback"
# 3) 把它追加到 profile 的 dsh.profile.bundles 末尾
#    （放最后 = 它的 `- id: web` 覆盖在官方 anysearch 之后生效）
# 4) 在 profile 的 node_modules 下建同名入口（本机既有形状：真目录 + 硬链接）
# 5) 重启 DSH —— 新开一个对话不够，profile 的配置树是启动时组合的
```

本插件的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会 `insert` 自己的 bundle（id `dsh-anysearch-fallback`），并把 web 服务的 `fetchProvider` 覆盖为 `anysearch-fallback`（`searchProvider` 必须一起原样写上——patch 对 `config` 是整体替换、不深合并）。具体层内覆盖请按你的 profile 现状调整。

### 测试

```bash
npm test            # 离线单测：63 通过 / 1 跳过（联网用例默认跳过）
```

`test/integration.test.mjs` 是**联网实测**用例（真实 422 → 真实直抓）：它需要 `@anysearch/anysearch-dsh` 及其 peer 包可被解析。仓库内默认跳过；在本机已装好的环境里可按该文件头部的注释搭一个临时 staging 目录（`node_modules` 里为 `@deepseek-ai/*` 建 junction）后运行。

### 已知边界 / 未做

- **DNS rebinding 只防一半**：除字面 IP / 主机名判定外，会在 DNS 解析后再核一遍解析到的 IP（任一解析结果非公网即拒）；但**没有地址钉扎** —— 校验用的解析结果与真正建连之间有时间差（TOCTOU），极端的 rebinding 仍可能穿过。
  *(对比：`dsh-web` 自带的 `dsh-web-fetch-http` 用 `ipaddr.js` + undici pinned agent 做了完整钉扎；本插件刻意零依赖，故未复刻。)*
- **带 userinfo 的 URL 会被拒绝**：`http://user:pw@example.com/`（只给用户名也算）一律以 `WEB_BLOCKED_URL` 拒掉，错误消息里点名 userinfo；**不做静默剥离** —— 用户显式给了带凭证的 URL 就明确报错，比悄悄改写更可预测。
- **保守拒绝**：`168.63/16`、`198.18/15`、`192.0.0/24` 等非公网段被判为内网并拒绝，宁可误拒。
- **提取质量**：朴素 HTML 降噪（去 script/style、取标题、解实体、折叠空白），质量低于 AnySearch 的正文清洗；结果顶部有降级标记，便于人工/模型识别。
- **系统性问题现在也会降级（这是宽兜底的代价）**：上游 401（凭据失效）、402（额度耗尽）、429（限流）这类问题**不再整次报错**，而是静默降级为直抓结果 —— 直抓往往仍能成功，于是"接口已经不可用了，但抓取照常返回"。要判断集成是否正常，看**正文首行的标记**（里面写明上游错误，例如 `上游错误（HTTP 429 rate limit）：…`）与日志里的 `warn` 行。
- **不做重试**：无论上游还是直抓都不重试。
- **不改超时预算**：`web_fetch` 工具预算 30 s 由 DSH 工具层硬编码，本插件不碰；兜底直抓自带 15 s，若上游已耗尽大部分预算，兜底可能来不及完成。
- **非 2xx 不假装成功**：直抓拿到 4xx/5xx 时按真实状态码返回（并保留正文）。
- **反爬限制**：目标站可能对匿名直抓返回 403 或直接给反爬页（例：`openai.com` 返回 403 且正文为空；知乎问题页返回 403 + 一句反爬文案）。此时降级正文可能为空或根本不是真正文 —— 标记行会把这种情况说清楚（含"站点未返回任何正文内容"），但拿不到内容就是拿不到，建议换来源。
- **改完必须重启 DSH**：已启动的 DSH 进程加载的是启动时的代码；升级或改动本插件（包括只改了降级标记文案）后，**必须重启 DSH**（新开一个对话不够）新代码才生效。

### License

MIT

---

## English

**Problem.** `web_fetch` goes through AnySearch `/v1/extract`; for some pages the upstream answers **HTTP 422 `extract_failed`** and the whole fetch call fails. This plugin registers its own `anysearch-fallback` fetch provider, points the web service at it, delegates to the official `anysearch` provider first, and degrades to a guarded direct fetch on **any** upstream failure — the only exception is cancellation.

**Guarantees.**

- Success path unchanged, field for field.
- Cancellation (`signal` aborted, `AbortError`, `ABORT_ERR` / `WEB_ABORTED` / `extract_canceled`, abort/cancel wording) is never degraded: the original error surfaces untouched and no new request is sent.
- Any other upstream failure (401/402/403/429/timeouts/network) degrades, and the reason is written into the first line of the returned body plus a `warn` log line — never silently swallowed.
- Only `http:`/`https:`; localhost, private, link-local, CGNAT and IPv4-mapped IPv6 targets are refused.
- A URL carrying userinfo (`user:pw@host`) is refused as `WEB_BLOCKED_URL` and named as such — never silently stripped.
- Hard 5 MB byte cap read as a stream (`response.body`), never `response.text()`; character cap matches DSH's tool layer.
- 15 s own timeout chained to the upstream abort signal.
- Fixed desktop Chrome UA plus `accept`/`accept-language`; no Authorization, Cookie, Referer; no TLS bypass; no disk cache.
- Manual redirects, at most 3 hops, re-validated at every hop.
- Fallback output carries a visible marker line naming both real statuses, so a degraded result is never mistaken for cleaned text and an empty body is never mistaken for an empty page.

**Not done.** No address pinning after resolution (one re-check, then a separate connect — TOCTOU remains), no retry, no timeout-budget change, naive HTML reduction (lower quality than AnySearch extraction). Anti-bot sites may answer 403 with an empty body or a challenge page: the marker says so, but there is no content to return — change the source instead.

**Cost of the broad fallback.** Systemic upstream problems (401 credentials, 402 quota, 429 rate limit) now degrade instead of failing the call, so a broken integration can still return pages. Watch the marker line (it names the upstream error) and the `warn` log line.

**Restart required.** A running DSH process keeps the code it booted with; restart DSH after changing this plugin (a new chat is not enough).

**Test.** `npm test` — 63 passed / 1 skipped offline. The network integration test is skipped unless the installed official bundle and its peer packages are resolvable.

*

把解除武装的会话目标重新武装（重启/session-start edge 后的 rearm）——补上 goal 自动续跑被中断的缺口

plugins.description: Collapsible provider groups and prominent provider headings for the DSH (DeepSeek Harness) model selection menu.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-provider-fold

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold)

Collapsible provider groups with prominent headings for the **DSH (DeepSeek Harness)** model selection menu.

When several providers are connected, the model picker becomes one long scroll. This plugin turns every provider heading into a clickable disclosure row with a stronger visual style, and lets you fold the providers you are not using.

![dsh-provider-fold in the DSH model menu](./docs/screenshot.png)

## Features

- **Collapsible provider groups** — click a provider heading (or focus it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>) to fold that provider's models away.
- **Prominent provider headings** — headings are upgraded from 11px/500 tertiary text to a 12px/600 primary-label row with a chevron, so providers are easy to scan.
- **Model count badge** — a folded provider shows how many models it hides.
- **Remembers your choice** — folded providers are stored in `localStorage` and restored the next time you open the menu.
- **Search always wins** — typing in the search box expands everything so matches are never hidden; your saved folding is untouched and comes back when you clear the search.
- **Keyboard friendly** — moving the highlight into a folded provider reveals it for that interaction only, without overwriting what you saved.
- **Scoped and defensive** — only the model menu (`role="menu"` + `-models` container) is decorated; any other menu built from the same primitives is left alone. If the host markup changes, the plugin does nothing instead of breaking the menu.
- **No layout removal** — folding hides rows with `display: none` and keeps them in the DOM, so the host component's own keyboard index stays correct.

## Install

Install straight from this repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

Replace `web` with the profile you use (for the desktop app that is usually `desktop`):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

The same target also works as a full URL if your setup prefers it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/rnmxrbb/dsh-provider-fold
```

After installing, reload the page once. The plugin is a client-side bundle with `immediately: true`, so it mounts with the app shell.

To remove it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-provider-fold
```

## Usage

1. Open the model menu in the composer (the model chip).
2. Each provider name is now a heading row with a chevron.
3. Click a heading, or focus it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd>, to fold or unfold that provider.
4. Folded providers show a small count of the models they contain.

## Compatibility

- DSH client `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer.
- `platform: "web"` only (the desktop app uses the web surface).
- Uses only public, stable hooks exposed by the host UI: `data-menu-group` / `data-menu-group-heading` on the primitives `MenuGroup`, plus DSH theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-label-primary`, `--dsw-alias-label-caption`, `--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-hover`, `--dsw-alias-border-l2`, `--dsw-focus-ring-color`).
- No host services, no network access, no telemetry. The only persisted data is the list of folded provider names in `localStorage` under the key `dsh-provider-fold:collapsed`.

## Permissions

| Resource | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `localStorage` | Store which providers you folded. |
| DOM (read/write) | Decorate the model menu and toggle `display` on model rows. |

Nothing else is touched.

## How it works

The plugin ships a client bundle and a host bundle:

- `client.js` — a DSH client module. Inside `apply(ctx)` it registers a single `ctx.effect` that injects one `<style data-plugin="dsh-provider-fold">` element, installs a `MutationObserver` plus delegated `click` / `keydown` / `input` / `focusin` listeners, and returns a cleanup function. The host's client-modules runtime claims the style element and removes it automatically on reload or uninstall.
- `index.js` — an empty host half (`export function apply() {}`) so the bundle has a resolvable entry point.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — inserts the bundle into the profile composition.

## Development

The repository root *is* the plugin package. To hack on it against a live DSH install:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-provider-fold
```

That installs it as a link, so edits to `client.js` are picked up by the host's client HMR watcher within about half a second — no host restart and no page refresh needed.

Run the headless DOM test suite (jsdom) that covers decoration, folding, persistence, search interaction, keyboard reveal and teardown:

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

# dsh-agent-sister

**一句话**：管理**孪生妹妹**（DSH 桌面端 / Electron）的生命周期——启动、停止、重启、查状态，并带 CDP 调试端口以便后续做 DOM 级驱动。 **为什么值得用**：桌面端是**独立进程树**（Electron 常留僵尸进程），「进程在不在」与「服务活不活」是两件事。本插件的判活判据是 **CDP 能应答**，不是 `tasklist` 里有没有那个名字——所以它不会把僵尸进程报成「alive」，也不会把正在启动报成「死了」（返回 `alive` / `starting` / `stopped` 三态）。 ## 能力 **工具面 4 个**（名称逐字来自 `src/index.ts` 的 `defineTool({ name })`）： | 工具 | 用途 | |------|------| | `sister_status` | 查状态：进程数 · **CDP 可达性** · 她的版本 · 判活裁决（`alive` / `starting` / `stopped`） | | `sister_start` | 启动（带 `--remote-debugging-port`，默认 9333）以便后续 `webops_attach` 做 DOM 操作。**已在跑则不动**（幂等） | | `sister_stop` | 停止**全部**进程。⚠ 她是庄园成员，停她会中断她手上的活——主人在直接使用她时先问一声 | | `sister_restart` | 先停后起（用于让 profile 配置改动生效——她的 profile 是 Electron 独占的，改配置后**必须重启**才会重新读） | ## 快速开始 **1) 装依赖**： ```jsonc "dsh-agent-sister": "link:E:/alice/self-plugins/dsh-agent-sister" ``` **2) 挂组合**： ```yaml - id: sister name: dsh-agent-sister config: cdpPort: 9333 ``` **3) 30 秒验证**：`sister_status` → 应返回三态之一 + CDP 可达性；`sister_start {wait: true}` → 应等到 CDP 就绪才返回；再 `sister_status` → 应报 `alive`。 ## 配置 | 项 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `cdpPort` | `9333` | 远程调试端口（供 `webops_attach` 附着做 DOM 级驱动） | ## 落盘与自证 **本插件无持久产物**——它管理的是**外部进程**，状态由 `sister_status` **现读**（进程表 + CDP 探测），不缓存、不落盘。 **判据**：`sister_status` 一条命令答「进程几个 / CDP 通不通 / 她什么版本 / 该算 alive 还是 stopped」。 ## 生效判据与回退 **判据**：行为级——`sister_status` 返回三态且与事实一致（可对照 `tasklist` 与 CDP 端口）。 **回退**：① `git revert` + 重建 + 预检重启；② patch 行 `disabled: true`；③ 停用插件**不影响**她继续运行（插件只是遥控器）。 ## 测试 ```bash cd self-plugins/dsh-agent-sister && npm test ``` **6 条用例**（跑一次得到）：覆盖三态判活裁决（**CDP 应答优先于进程存在**）· 幂等启动（已在跑不动）· 版本读取失败时的退化路径。无需网络。 ## 设计要点 - **判活判据 = CDP 能应答**，不是「进程存在」——Electron 的僵尸进程会让「进程数 > 0」恒为真，那是**假活**。 - **三态而非二态**：`starting` 是独立一态——启动中既不是 `alive` 也不是 `stopped`，合并任何一边都会误导。 - **幂等启动**：已在跑则不动（避免「再起一个」造成多实例）。 - **重启是为配置生效**：她的 profile 由 Electron 独占，改配置**必须重启**才重新读——这不是实现选择，是宿主行为。 - **她是成员不是我的分身**：停她会中断她的活——调用前先问（庄园成员是对等存在）。 ## 相关文档 - ⚠ **本插件暂无 `semantic.md`**（未建语义文档）——契约以上面「设计要点」与源码为准；补文档是待办。 - 中心仓：[alice-digital-life](https://github.com/jonah791/alice-digital-life)（本插件归 **生命层**） - 相关插件：[`dsh-manor`](https://github.com/jonah791/dsh-manor)（庄园成员调度）、[`dsh-agent-webops`](https://github.com/jonah791/dsh-agent-webops)（`webops_attach` 附着她的 CDP 做界面驱动） ## License MIT © jonah791 --- 本插件属于**爱丽丝 DSH 自研插件生态**（[alice-digital-life](https://github.com/jonah791/alice-digital-life) · 73 个插件 · 8 个模块）：单一职责、独立仓库、独立可用。

plugins.description: Vendor marks in the DeepSeek Harness model picker: the provider's own model catalog and logos mirrored to a loopback route, painted with a CSS mask in the composer menu, the model button and the /model popup.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-model-icons

Vendor marks in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI model picker — the same marks the
provider's own dashboard draws next to each model, in the same way it draws them.

| Surface | What appears |
|---|---|
| Composer model menu | one 16 px monochrome mark before every model row |
| Composer model button | the selected model's mark before its name (14 px) |
| `/model` command popup | the same mark on every row |
| A skin that redraws the picker (`dsh-claude-style`) | the same mark, and the skin's own lockup is hidden in that row so two never meet |

The marks are painted with a CSS mask filled by `currentColor`, which is how the
provider's dashboard paints them: one file per vendor serves both palettes and
every row state (hover, selected, disabled) with no colour variants.

## Where the pictures come from

Nothing is embedded in this package. The host half mirrors two public things from
the provider's site into this profile, and the browser half reads them from
loopback:

1. **the model catalog** — the site renders its model table from a JSON island in
   its own page (`<script id="rustvy-catalog">`), so an unauthenticated reader is
   handed exactly the data the dashboard shows: model id, display name, vendor
   and the logo file name that vendor uses. Mirrored to
   `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\catalog.json`.
2. **the logo files** (`/logos/<name>.svg`) — copied into
   `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\logos\` on first use.

Both are read on the process's own outbound route (`lib/net.js`): the live global
dispatcher first, so a proxy installed by `dsh-proxy-gui` — or any other route the
process has — is followed, and a connector built here from `HTTPS_PROXY` /
`ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` second, for the case where no dispatcher is installed.
`NO_PROXY` is honoured on both. The page itself never leaves the machine: the
browser asks `127.0.0.1` for a mark, which is what makes this work on a machine
whose browser cannot reach the origin at all.

The catalog refreshes once every 24 hours and on demand; a cold mirror is waited
for up to 6 seconds, and a stale one refreshes in the background while the rows
keep the marks they have. When the origin is unreachable, the cache on disk still
serves everything it holds.

## Matching a row to a mark

Rows are matched by their visible name, in this order:

1. the mirrored catalog's model id (`claude-opus-5-5`, `abyss/glm-5.3`, …);
2. its display name (`OPUS 5.5`);
3. an id the label *starts* with — a skin can leave its own description line in
   the same element, so the name is often a prefix rather than the whole string,
   and the longest matching id wins so `claude-opus-5-5` is never claimed by
   `claude-opus-5`;
4. the shape of the id, for a model the mirror has never seen: `claude-*` →
   Anthropic, `gpt-*`/`o1…o9` → OpenAI, `glm-*` → Zhipu, `kimi-*`/`k3` →
   Moonshot, `qwen-*` → Alibaba Qwen, `deepseek-*` → DeepSeek, `ahmia-*` → Ahmia,
   `mimo-*` → Xiaomi, `fable-*` → Anthropic, `gemini-*` → Google, `grok-*` → xAI.

A model that matches nothing gets no mark at all — an invented icon would be a
wrong answer rather than a missing one. A model that matches but whose logo the
mirror could not fetch gets a monogram chip (the vendor's first letters) instead
of a blank box: a mask whose URL 404s would otherwise paint a solid square.

Effort rows, provider headings, the menu's root cells, the search field and
catalog-failure rows are matched by nothing and stay bare.

## Routes

One prefix registration on the harness's own web server. Plugin routes are not
seen by the host's request fence, so every one of them checks the peer itself:
loopback only, a loopback `Host`, a same-origin `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a matching
`Origin`.

| Route | Method | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `/dsh-model-icons/catalog.json` | GET | the mirrored catalog plus the settings the browser half draws with |
| `/dsh-model-icons/logo/<name>.svg` | GET, HEAD | one cached logo, fetched from the origin on first ask; `404` when the origin has no such mark, `400` for any name that is not `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+.svg` |
| `/dsh-model-icons/state` | GET | mirror status for the settings page: version, model count, cached logos, route, proxy (credentials masked), cache directory, last error |
| `/dsh-model-icons/refresh` | POST | re-read the catalog and re-warm every logo it names |
| `/dsh-model-icons/config` | POST | write settings; never touches the network |

## Settings

**Settings → Иконки моделей**

| Switch | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Показывать иконки моделей | on | master switch; off removes every mark |
| Иконка в кнопке выбранной модели | on | also mark the composer's model button, not just the menu rows |
| Прятать логотипы других скинов | on | hide a skin's own lockup in a row this plugin marked |

The page also shows what the mirror holds and refreshes it on demand.

Stored in `<profile>\.dsh-model-icons\config.json`. Two environment variables
override it, for a deployment that points the mirror elsewhere or wants the
plugin mounted but inert: `DSH_MODEL_ICONS_ORIGIN` (default `https://rustvy.xyz`)
and `DSH_MODEL_ICONS_DISABLED=1`. The mark size is a config field (`size`,
10–32 px, default 16).

## No restarts

The host half reloads itself, the same way `dsh-proxy-gui` does: the loader row
names `./lib/live.js`, which imports the implementation through a cache-busting
`?rev=` query, and a one-second poll of the `lib` directory disposes the previous
revision and starts the next one once a changed fingerprint repeats. The browser
half arrives in an open page through the harness's own live plugin composition;
a page refresh works too.

## Install

```powershell
pwsh -File .\install.ps1
```

Copies the package into `<profile>\node_modules\dsh-model-icons` as a real
directory, regenerates `lib/live.js` from `lib/index.js` so the two cannot drift,
and appends the package to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. A
running harness picks the row up from the manifest change.

Uninstall: remove the name from `dsh.profile.bundles`, delete
`<profile>\node_modules\dsh-model-icons`, and delete
`<profile>\.dsh-model-icons` if you also want the cache gone.

## Layout

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | stable loader entry; owns the reload loop |
| `lib/live.js` | byte-identical copy of the entry, named by the loader row |
| `lib/host.js` | routes, catalog mirror, logo cache, settings |
| `lib/net.js` | one outbound GET on the process's route, then the environment's proxy |
| `client/client.js` | hand-authored browser bundle: the decorator and the settings page |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | the loader row the profile's bundle list pulls in |
| `install.ps1` | install into a profile |

## Tests

Both halves are covered without touching the running app:

```powershell
node _probe\model-icons-host-test.mjs      # host: fake webServer, real origin fetch
node _probe\dom-test\model-icons-client-test.mjs   # browser: linkedom + stubbed mirror
```

The host test drives the registered route with fake request/response pairs and
asserts the catalog answer, a real logo fetch, `404` for a mark the origin does
not have, `400` for a traversal attempt, `403` for a non-loopback peer, `405` for
a wrong method, and the on-disk cache. The client test builds the exact markup
the harness menu, the `/model` popup and the skin render, and asserts which rows
get a mark, which icon each gets, that effort rows and headings stay bare, that
the monogram fallback appears for a missing logo, that a row added later is
picked up by the observer, that a pass is idempotent, and that an unload removes
every trace.

plugins.description: Ctrl+wheel page zoom for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI, with an on-screen zoom chip and a General settings row.
plugins.readme_text:
# Ctrl + Wheel Zoom

Hold **Ctrl** (or **⌘** on macOS) and roll the mouse wheel to zoom the whole Harness Web UI.
A page-zoom plugin for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web GUI, distributed as an ordinary
DSH **profile bundle**: no build step, no runtime dependency, plain ESM.

## What it does

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + wheel | Zooms the page around the pointer, 50%–200%, in 10% steps |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `+` / `-` | Same from the keyboard |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `0` | Back to 100% |
| Zoom chip (bottom-right) | Appears whenever the level is not 100%: click the percentage to reset, click **Fit to width** to fit the window |
| Settings → General | A **Page zoom** row with the host's stepper pattern and a reset button |

The chosen level is remembered in the browser (`localStorage`), and every listener, stylesheet and
the applied `zoom` property are removed when the plugin is disabled or unloaded.

A gesture that another component already handled (`preventDefault()`, e.g. an embedded code editor
or map with its own `Ctrl`+wheel zoom) is never stolen.

## Install

Ask the Harness agent to install it, or call the plugin manager yourself with the package located
by absolute path, a tarball, or a published name:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: <absolute path to this package / a .tgz / a published name>
```

`install_bundle` links the package into the active profile (`$DSH_PROFILE_DIR`), adds it to the
profile's bundle list, and the Harness applies it live. A page refresh picks up the browser half in
a page that was already open.

To install it by hand instead, add the package to the profile's dependencies and to
`dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/package.json`, then restart the Harness.

## Uninstall

```
plugin_manager  action: remove_bundle
                target: dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom
```

## Requirements

- A Harness Web GUI (the client half declares `platform: "web"`; it is inert without a browser).
- Nothing else: the package has no dependencies, no build output, and no install scripts. Built-in
  client modules (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`) come from the shell's own module table.

## Sharing and publishing

The package is self-contained, so there are three ways to hand it to someone else.

### 1. A tarball

```bash
pnpm pack                        # writes dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom-1.0.0.tgz
```

Send that `.tgz`; the receiver installs it by path:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: <path to dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom-1.0.0.tgz>
```

(`pnpm pack` writes the tarball beside `package.json`. DSH's own runtime ships a pnpm, so nothing
has to be installed first.)

### 2. The directory (zip / repository)

Zip this folder (or push it to a Git repository) and have the receiver install the **unpacked
directory** by path — `install_bundle` accepts a directory, and a folder is enough because there is
no build step.

### 3. npm (install by name for everyone)

This manifest is already publishable: `name` is the unscoped `dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom`, the row in
`cordis.patch.yml` names the same specifier, and there is no `"private": true`.

npm no longer issues long-lived "classic" tokens — they were permanently revoked on 2025-12-09 —
and publishing requires two-factor authentication. Pick one of the two ways through:

```bash
# A. A granular access token created with "Bypass two-factor authentication" enabled,
#    stored once as a credential:
#      //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=npm_...        in ~/.npmrc
pnpm publish --no-git-checks

# B. Any write token, with a one-time password supplied per publish:
pnpm publish --no-git-checks --otp=<6-digit code>
```

A token without bypass-2FA is refused with `403 ... Two-factor authentication or granular access
token with bypass 2fa enabled is required to publish packages`. Verify what a token can actually do
before blaming the command:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/tokens
#   "bypass_2fa": false   → use --otp, or recreate the token with the switch on
#   "permissions": [{"name":"package","action":"write"}]   → publishing is permitted at all
```

Note npm's stated direction: bypass-2FA tokens are on a path to removal (targeted for January 2027)
in favour of staged publishing or trusted publishing, so a long-lived automated release will need
one of those later.

Keep `name` in `package.json` and the `name:` line of `cordis.patch.yml` identical in every
release — the loader resolves the row through that specifier. Bump `version` for each release.

Afterwards anyone installs it by name:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: dsh-ctrl-wheel-zoom
```

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: an empty `apply()`; the row exists so the bundle can be installed and toggled |
| `client.js` | Browser half: wheel/keyboard gestures, zoom state, chip and settings-row registrations, stylesheets |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The loader patch that inserts the `ctrl-wheel-zoom` row |
| `locale/{zh,en}.json` | Plugin-card title/description text; the row's own copy lives in `client.js` |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin-manager card artwork |

## How the zoom works

Zoom is CSS `zoom` on the document element. It scales layout, text and fixed overlay layers
together exactly like the browser's own page zoom, while the app's own scroll containers keep
working — a `transform: scale()` wrapper cannot scroll its oversized content, and a font-size
change would only touch text.

The wheel listener is registered in the capture phase on `window`, so it sees the gesture before
the app's scroll containers and blocks them from scrolling while `Ctrl` is held. When the viewport
itself scrolls, the plugin re-anchors it so the content under the pointer stays under the pointer.

Both UI surfaces read one store instance shared with the gesture writer, so the chip, the settings
stepper and the wheel listener can never disagree about the current level.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

plugins.description: Session cost and billing metrics for the DSH Web GUI: what this conversation cost, what the cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. A companion to the shipped stats pills, never a duplicate of them.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-metrics

Session **cost and billing** metrics for the DSH Web GUI — what this conversation cost, what the
cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. Built as a companion to the shipped
stats pills, never a duplicate of them.

## Why

The shipped stats pills report tokens and context, and stop short of money. That leaves three
questions unanswered, and the obvious answer to each is a lie:

**A model with no rate card is not free.** An unpriceable provider reads `unpriced` and shows its
tokens; a genuinely free model ships a card of zeros and reads a real `$0.00`. The two must not
render alike — `unpriced` means *no card*, and an unpriced pair is never rendered as a number.

**A newly integrated provider arrives silently.** DSH reports usage per provider and model; rates are
configuration. Integrate a provider before its rates are entered — the case that happened with
OpenRouter — and every figure for it is missing with nothing on the page saying why. The session
detail names the pair it observed with no card, and the tokens it used.

**Peak pricing is invisible until it is a surprise.** DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak at different
rates, in the provider's own timezone. Whether *right now* is peak is not something a user should
have to derive.

## Agent Skills

Installing the plugin registers the **`session-metrics`** skill, so an agent can explain the figures
and reconfigure the rates without reading the source. Ask it what a session cost, whether a model is
priced, or how to add a rate card for a provider it has seen.

## Quick Start

The plugin installs into your DSH **profile** by link — it is not published to npm, so the clone is
the source. Both routes end with a **restart**.

### Option A — the script

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
./install.sh                 # builds, registers in your profile, runs pnpm install
```

It accepts `--profile <dir>` to target a profile other than `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`, `--check` to
report what would change without writing anything, and `--remove` to unregister.

### Option B — the manual steps

**1. Clone it somewhere stable** (this path becomes your install path):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
```

**2. Build it.** `pnpm install` runs the `prepare` script, which builds `lib/**` — the part DSH
actually loads. It is generated; never hand-edit it.

```bash
pnpm install
```

**3. Register it with your profile** — the dependency and the bundle name, with an absolute path:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-session-metrics": "link:/Users/<you>/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        "dsh-session-metrics"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**4. Install the link, then restart DSH:**

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && pnpm install
```

Nothing needs adding to `cordis.patch.yml`: the bundle declares its own Loader row.

> **Restart, don't reload.** The host half loads once per app process, so a host-side change needs a
> full quit and reopen (`⌘Q`, then reopen). A page reload does not pick it up. A client-side (UI)
> change needs the bundle toggled in the plugin manager.

### Verify it is really working

A strip should appear below the composer with `cost`, `saved` and a peak indicator. If it does not:

- `lib/v1/index.js` exists — if not, `pnpm install` did not finish building;
- the profile's `package.json` names `dsh-session-metrics` in **both** `dependencies` and
  `dsh.profile.bundles`;
- DSH was **restarted** after installing.

An `unpriced` chip means a working install with no matching rate card — not a failure. See
[Configure](#configure).

### Configure

**A fresh install needs no configuration.** Rate cards ship for `deepseek-account`,
`deepseek-official`, `netra-runtime` and `openrouter`, so the cost chip works immediately. OpenRouter
ships **only the models its own catalog marks free** (the `:free` suffix and the free-models router)
at zero rates; its paid models deliberately carry no card, because DSH reports no prices for them and
a fabricated rate is worse than a named gap.

Rates are edited in the GUI: **Plugins sidebar → `dsh-session-metrics`**. The same table can be set
in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: session-metrics
  name: dsh-session-metrics
  config:
    display: { currency: USD, primaryProvider: deepseek-account }
    budget: { sessionUsd: 5, warnAt: 0.75 }
    providers:
      - id: my-router
        models:
          - model: some/model
            rates: { flat: { cacheHit: 0.01, cacheMiss: 0.1, output: 0.25 } }
        billing: { windows: [] }      # no peak concept
```

Rates are USD per 1M tokens. A model takes **either** a `flat` row **or** a `peak` row with
`offPeak`. A provider with no `billing.windows` is flat and shows no peak chip.

> **A `providers:` list in your patch replaces the shipped cards** rather than adding to them. Pin your
> own providers and the OpenRouter free cards stop shipping with them — add a card for each pair you
> need, or let **Seen, unpriced** name the ones you missed.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `display.currency` | `USD` | `USD` or `CNY` |
| `display.primaryProvider` | — | hides the provider chip when the session uses this provider |
| `display.chips` | all | which chips to show, and in what order: `peak`, `time`, `cost`, `saved`, `provider`, `budget` |
| `budget.sessionUsd` | off | per-session ceiling; omit to disable |
| `budget.warnAt` | `0.75` | fraction of the budget at which the strip warns |

The full rate-card format, the shipped cards and the reasoning behind them are in
[`docs/pricing.md`](docs/pricing.md).

## How it Works

Costs are derived from the Host's own `tokenUsage` projection — the same source the stats pills read
— so this plugin adds interpretation, not a second ledger. Cache savings compare each cache-hit token
against the rate that would have been paid on a miss, per the card in effect. Peak and off-peak
windows resolve in the provider's own timezone, holidays included, and the countdown is computed once
a minute while the detail view is open rather than on every render.

Two surfaces, one projection:

- **the strip**, below the composer: cost, cache savings, the peak state with your local time, the
  provider when it is not your configured primary, and budget progress;
- **the detail**, on click: the cost breakdown (cache-hit / miss / write / output), cache savings and
  blended rate, the rate window with a countdown, cost per step, cost per model when a session
  switched models, and the projections each figure came from.

The plugin deliberately does **not** render session token totals, cache-hit rate, context percentage,
turns, steps or tok/s — the shipped pills own those. [`docs/data-sources.md`](docs/data-sources.md)
records which projection feeds which figure, which is what keeps the two from drifting back into
duplication.

### Requirements

- **DSH** with the Web GUI, and a profile you can edit (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/`).
- **Node.js 22+** and **pnpm** to build from source. The built artifact needs nothing extra at
  runtime.

### Development

```bash
pnpm install                  # deps + build (prepare)
pnpm run build                # rebuild lib/**
pnpm test                     # 111 tests: 105 pass, 6 skipped without a session log
pnpm run typecheck            # three projects: host, browser half, tests
pnpm run test:fast            # host logic only — the quick loop
pnpm run test:dom             # the UI half under jsdom
DSH_SESSION_LOG=<path>.jsonl.zstd pnpm run test:replay   # replays a real session
```

```
src/host/*.ts         host half: config schema, projection, ledger, pricing  -> lib/v1/index.js
src/client/index.cts  browser half: strip, detail panel, pricing page        -> lib/v1/client.js
types/dsh.d.ts        the DSH surfaces this plugin uses (the app ships no .d.ts)
build.mjs             esbuild: ESM host half, CJS browser half + loader h
